description: Every file-based source the panel is meant to handle, side by side: GeoParquet through DuckDB, GeoJSON and CSV through Infinity. Each panel is deliberately unconfigured — no saved mapConfig — so what renders is what autodetection alone produces.

options.content:
# Fuentes de datos

Cada panel llega al mismo sitio — una capa de kepler — por un camino distinto. Ninguno tiene capas guardadas: lo que se dibuja es lo que la autodetección deduce de las columnas. Lo único fijado es el encuadre, porque sin él el mapa arranca demasiado cerca y parte del dataset queda fuera de pantalla.

| Panel | Origen | Cómo llega la geometría |
|---|---|---|
| GeoParquet · puntos | DuckDB `read_parquet` | columnas `latitude` / `longitude` |
| GeoParquet · zonas | DuckDB + extensión `spatial` | `ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_GeomFromWKB(...))` |
| GeoJSON · zonas | Infinity, URL | objeto `geometry` serializado a string |
| CSV · puntos | Infinity, URL | convención `<prefijo>_latitude` de kepler |
| CSV · zonas | Infinity, URL | WKT en una columna `geometry` |

Los ficheros salen de `testdata/`, servidos por el contenedor `sources-data` y montados en `/testdata` dentro de Grafana.

panels.description: Plain columns, no spatial extension involved. The parquet carries point_latitude/point_longitude alongside the geometry, and aliasing them to latitude/longitude is what the plugin's own detectFields matches on.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  name,
  category,
  visitors,
  point_latitude  AS latitude,
  point_longitude AS longitude
FROM read_parquet('/testdata/cuenca-points.parquet')

panels.title: GeoParquet · puntos (DuckDB)

panels.description: kepler reads no form of WKB, so the geometry has to become GeoJSON. Note there is no ST_GeomFromWKB call: DuckDB's spatial extension reads a GeoParquet geometry column as a native GEOMETRY (carrying its EPSG:4326 CRS), not as a BLOB. The CAST to VARCHAR is not decoration — ST_AsGeoJSON returns DuckDB's JSON type and the data source's Go driver cannot Scan that into a string.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  name,
  population,
  CAST(ST_AsGeoJSON(geometry) AS VARCHAR) AS geojson
FROM read_parquet('/testdata/cuenca-zones.parquet')

panels.title: GeoParquet · zonas (DuckDB + spatial)

panels.description: A GeoJSON URL flattened by Infinity's backend parser. Typing the geometry column as String is what makes Infinity serialise the nested object to a GeoJSON string; the panel then autodetects the geojson column as geometry.
panels.title: GeoJSON · zonas (Infinity, URL)

panels.description: The lat/lng columns keep kepler's <prefix>_latitude naming, which the plugin's detectFields does NOT match — it renders anyway because kepler runs its own layer autodetection and that convention is one of its own. Infinity's CSV parser types every column as string, hence the explicit Number types.
panels.title: CSV · puntos (Infinity, URL)

panels.description: Geometry embedded in the CSV as WKT. kepler's geojson layer reads WKT strings directly, so no conversion is needed anywhere in the chain.
panels.title: CSV · zonas en WKT (Infinity, URL)

title: Fuentes — GeoParquet, GeoJSON y CSV
